title: Outcome Measures — Is the Change Real and Does It Matter?

hook.en: A patient's score went from 20 to 18. Is that progress, or noise? Learn to choose an outcome measure, read a change score and use the minimal important change so you can show patients and others that treatment is working.
hook.ur: Mareez ka score 20 se 18 hua. Kya yeh progress hai ya shor? Outcome measure chunna, change score parhna aur minimal important change istemal karna seekhein taake aap mareezon aur doosron ko dikha sakein ke ilaj kaam kar raha hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll choose a validated measure for pain, disability or function, record a baseline, calculate change, and judge it against measurement error and the minimal important change.
goal.ur: End tak aap dard, disability ya function ke liye validated measure chunenge, baseline likhenge, change nikalenge, aur use measurement error aur minimal important change se parkhenge.

text.en: An **outcome measure** puts a patient's pain, function or quality of life into a number you can track. Use measures that are **valid** (measure what they claim), **reliable** (give the same answer if nothing has changed) and **responsive** (notice real change). Then ask: is the change bigger than the **measurement error**, and is it bigger than the **minimal important change (MIC)**, the smallest change a patient would call worth having?
text.ur: **Outcome measure** mareez ke dard, function ya zindagi ke maiyaar ko aise number mein badalta hai jis ki aap nigrani kar sakein. Aise measures istemal karein jo **valid** hon (jo daawa karein woh naapein), **reliable** hon (kuch na badle to wohi jawab dein) aur **responsive** hon (asli tabdeeli bhanp lein). Phir poochhein: kya tabdeeli **measurement error** se bari hai, aur **minimal important change (MIC)** se bari hai, yaani woh chhoti tareen tabdeeli jise mareez qabil-e-qadar kahe?

text.en: Think of a bathroom scale. If it jumps by half a kilo each time you step on and off, a half-kilo change tells you nothing: that is **measurement error**. And even a real change of 200 grams may not matter to you: that is below your **minimal important change**. An outcome measure works the same way.
text.ur: Ghusal khane ke wazan scale ko sochein. Agar har baar utarne chadhne par woh aadha kilo hil jaye to aadhe kilo ki tabdeeli kuch nahi batati: yeh **measurement error** hai. Aur 200 gram ki asli tabdeeli bhi aap ke liye ahem na ho: yeh aap ki **minimal important change** se kam hai. Outcome measure bhi isi tarah kaam karta hai.

steps.title: Choose with the patient
steps.detail: Pick a measure that fits the problem and the person: a pain scale, a back or neck questionnaire, a shoulder or knee score or a performance test. Ask what the patient wants to be able to do. || Mareez ke saath chunein

steps.title: Record a baseline
steps.detail: Score the first visit and give the same measure in the same way each time, with the same instructions. Note the date and any treatment started. || Baseline likhein

steps.title: Calculate the change
steps.detail: Subtract the baseline from the follow-up (taking care with the direction, since higher is better on some scales and worse on others). Convert to a percentage if the tool needs it. || Tabdeeli nikalein

steps.title: Judge the change
steps.detail: Compare it with the minimal important change and the measurement error for that tool and condition. Share the meaning with the patient in plain words. || Tabdeeli parkhein

question.en: Which statement describes the minimal important change?
question.ur: Kaun sa bayan minimal important change ki tareef hai?

feedback.ur: Chhoti tabdeeliyan shor ho sakti hain.

text.en: The change that is statistically significant
text.ur: Woh tabdeeli jo statistically significant ho

text.en: The smallest change that a patient would consider worthwhile
text.ur: Chhoti tareen tabdeeli jise mareez qabil-e-qadar samjhe

feedback.en: Yes — it is based on the patient's view of benefit.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh mareez ke faide ke nazariye par mabni hai.

title.en: Common measures for low back pain
title.ur: Kamar ke dard ke aam measures

rows.en: About 5 points (Roland-Morris) or 10 points or 30 percent (Oswestry)
rows.ur: Takreeban 5 points (Roland-Morris) ya 10 points ya 30 percent (Oswestry)

rows.en: Quick tracking of pain at each visit
rows.ur: Har visit par dard ki tez nigrani

rows.en: Tracking function and goals over weeks
rows.ur: Haftoon mein function aur maqasid ki nigrani

text.en: **Beat the noise, beat the threshold.** A change is real when it is bigger than the measurement error, and meaningful when it is bigger than the minimal important change. Report both ideas honestly.
text.ur: **Shor ko harao, hadd ko harao.** Tabdeeli asli hai jab woh measurement error se bari ho, aur maani khez hai jab minimal important change se bari ho. Dono khayalat imandari se batayein.

text.en: **Calling any improvement "progress".** A two-point rise on a 100-point scale may be noise, while a ten-point change may be real and valued. Use the thresholds for that tool, and also ask the patient whether they feel better.
text.ur: **Har behtari ko "progress" kehna.** 100 point ke scale par do point ka izafa shor ho sakta hai, jabke das point ki tabdeeli asli aur qabil-e-qadar ho sakti hai. Us tool ki hadood istemal karein, aur mareez se bhi poochhein ke kya woh behtar mehsoos karta hai.

question.en: A patient's numeric pain score falls from 7 to 6. How should you describe this?
question.ur: Mareez ka numeric dard score 7 se 6 hua. Isay kaise bayan karein?

feedback.en: It is just a small change.
One point is below the usual threshold.
feedback.ur: Ek point aam hadd se kam hai.

text.en: A small change that is below the usual important change; keep monitoring and discuss function
text.ur: Chhoti tabdeeli jo aam ahem tabdeeli se kam hai; nigrani jaari rakhein aur function par baat karein

feedback.en: Yes — about 2 points or 30 percent is usually needed.
feedback.ur: Haan — aam taur par takreeban 2 points ya 30 percent chahiye.

question.en: Which tool property tells you that it gives the same result when nothing has changed?
question.ur: Tool ki kaun si khaasiyat batati hai ke kuch na badle to wohi nateeja deta hai?

feedback.ur: Yeh tabdeeli bhanpne ke baare mein hai.

feedback.en: That is about measuring what it claims.
feedback.ur: Yeh woh naapne ke baare mein hai jo daawa karta hai.
Haan — reliability dohraye jaane ki salahiyat hai.

text.en: **Use the number as a conversation, not a verdict.** Show the chart to the patient: "Your disability score has dropped from 18 to 11, a change that is above the usual important change." Pair it with a goal that matters to them, and adjust the plan if there is no meaningful change after four to six weeks.
text.ur: **Number ko guftagu banayein, faisla nahi.** Chart mareez ko dikhayein: "Aap ka disability score 18 se 11 hua, jo aam ahem tabdeeli se zyada hai." Isay un ke ahem maqsad ke saath jorein, aur chaar se chhe haftay baad koi maani khez tabdeeli na ho to plan badlein.

question.en: Why should the same outcome measure be used at each visit?
question.ur: Har visit par wohi outcome measure kyun istemal karna chahiye?

answer.en: Different tools use different scales, wording and thresholds, so their scores cannot be compared directly. Repeating the same tool with the same instructions allows you to see change that comes from the patient rather than from the measure.
answer.ur: Mukhtalif tools mukhtalif scales, alfaz aur hadood istemal karte hain, is liye unke scores seedhe muqable mein nahi aa sakte. Wohi tool wohi hidayat ke saath dohrane se aap woh tabdeeli dekh sakte hain jo mareez se aati hai, measure se nahi.

beats.patient: A 45-year-old man with low back pain scores 16 on the Roland-Morris questionnaire at baseline and 13 at four weeks; his pain falls from 6 to 4. He says he is "a bit better" but still cannot play with his children.
beats.assessment: The Roland-Morris change of 3 is below the usual 5-point threshold, while the pain change reaches about 2 points; he reports little functional gain.
beats.treatment: Acknowledge the improvement, set a goal of lifting his child, adjust exercises towards that task and re-score in four weeks.
beats.reassess: At eight weeks his score is 9 and he can lift his child, which is a meaningful change.

text.en: **A score is never a reason to ignore red flags.** If the patient reports a new weakness, loss of bladder or bowel control, saddle numbness, fever, unexplained weight loss or severe night pain, act on these at once, whatever the questionnaire says. A high score may also need psychological support.
text.ur: **Score kabhi red flags nazar andaz karne ki wajah nahi.** Mareez nayi kamzori, peshab ya pakhane par qaboo khona, saddle sunn hona, bukhar, be-wajah wazan ka girna ya shadeed raat ka dard bataye to questionnaire kuch bhi kahe, foran kaarwai karein. Zyada score ko nafsiyati madad ki bhi zaroorat ho sakti hai.

summary.en: Choose a valid, reliable, responsive measure with the patient, record a baseline and repeat it in the same way.
summary.ur: Mareez ke saath valid, reliable, responsive measure chunein, baseline likhein aur usay isi tareeqe se dohrayein.

summary.en: A change is real if it is bigger than the measurement error and meaningful if it is bigger than the minimal important change.
summary.ur: Tabdeeli asli hai agar measurement error se bari ho aur maani khez hai agar minimal important change se bari ho.

summary.en: Typical thresholds in low back pain: about 2 points or 30 percent for pain, 5 points for Roland-Morris and 10 points for Oswestry.
summary.ur: Kamar ke dard mein aam hadood: dard ke liye takreeban 2 points ya 30 percent, Roland-Morris ke liye 5 points aur Oswestry ke liye 10 points.

front.en: What is the minimal important change?

back.en: The smallest change a patient would consider worthwhile.
back.ur: Chhoti tareen tabdeeli jise mareez qabil-e-qadar samjhe.

back.en: The random variation in a score when nothing has really changed.
back.ur: Score mein random tabdeeli jab asal mein kuch na badla ho.

front.en: What is a typical important change in pain on a 0 to 10 scale?
front.ur: 0 se 10 ke scale par dard mein aam ahem tabdeeli kya hai?

back.en: So scores are comparable over time.
back.ur: Taake scores waqt ke saath muqable ke qabil hon.

note.en: Measure and progress an exercise plan.
note.ur: Exercise plan ko naapein aur barhayein.
